newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say Rwandans took missing refugees. [CORRECTED 12:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say Rwandans took missing refugees. [CORRECTED 12:25 GMT]

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Friday former Rwandan Hutu troops and militiamen evacuated thousands of Rwandan refugees too weak to walk from a camp south of Kisangani.
Under heavy international pressure over their treatment of the Rwandan Hutu refugees, a top rebel adviser attacked the U.N. refugee agency (UNHCR) for not repatriating refugees sooner.

Moise Nyarugabi, an adviser to rebel leader Laurent Kabila, told a news conference aid workers could search the area south of Kisangani for the refugees evacuated from Kasese camp by Rwandan former troops and militiamen and send food aid to them.

"I can't say what became of the refugees. I don't know what refugees were unable to walk," said Nyarugabi, repeating the rebel version that refugees in Kasese camp were attacked this week by former Rwandan troops and Interahamwe militiamen.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR says up to 9,000 of the 55,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees who vanished from Kasese camp this week were in no condition to walk, including 2,500 badly malnourished children.
"This (attack on the refugees) wasn't something that the militia and the ex-FAR (former Rwandan armed forces) did by surprise. The attack was planned in advance," Nyarugabi said.
He said the refugees, who had trekked through east Zaire for six months should have been taken to Rwanda by UNHCR sooner.

The governor of Zaire's Eastern province, appointed with rebel blessing, delayed the start of a U.N. airlift of the estimated 100,000 refugees south of Kisangani on Sunday until May 5 (Corrects from April 5), citing a cholera epidemic.
But the World Health Organisation said the cholera outbreak at Kasese camp south of Kisangnai was not big enough to be classed as an epidemic and should not delay the refugee airlift.

Camps at Kasese, 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani, and Biaro, 45 km (25 miles) south of Kisangani, were sealed off from aid workers and journalists from Monday until a U.N. team visited Kasese on Thursday and found it empty.

The Tutsi-dominated rebels have seized more than half of Zaire since October. The Rwandan Hutus fled Rwanda in 1994 after Tutsi guerrillas ousted a Hutu administration blamed for the killing of up to a million Tutsis and Hutu moderates.

Zairean villagers said rebels killed hundreds of refugees at Kasese and used a bulldozer to bury the bodies in mass graves. They said a pitched battle with Rwandan former troops and militiamen among the refugees accompanied the slaughter.
The U.N. Security Council on Thursday harshly criticised the rebels for preventing aid from reaching the Hutu refugees and obstructing their return home to Rwanda.
The council called "in the strongest terms" on the rebels "to ensure unrestricted and safe access by all humanitarian relief agencies" and said it was alarmed by reports of massacres.
Rebels agreed to allow the U.N. mission to Kasese only after U.N. chief Kofi Annan said he was appalled by the "inhumanity" of their action which was killing the refugees by starvation.
